answer: Cross-epoch latency lattice.** Each identity is placed on a fixed schedule: its first traffic must arrive as a sparse train of probes, spaced across many epochs, forming a trellis of correlated send times. Validators keep one pending island per candidate and admit an identity only after its pattern survives repeated slot-matching against that lattice. An attacker can't accelerate this: each additional sybil must spend its own weeks of timed probes, one per epoch, and any burst collapses the spacing test. Cedar marks the epoch boundary where probation ends,
